content_record.title: Naked mole-rat cGAS rewires DNA repair: four amino acids that slow aging
content_record.editorial_body: A new study reveals how naked mole-rats evade a suppressive function of cGAS to enhance homologous recombination repair, offering a precise molecular lever for lifespan extension. Four amino acid changes in naked mole-rat cGAS weaken TRIM41 ubiquitination and P97 extraction. Prolonged chromatin retention boosts FANCI-RAD50 interaction, accelerating RAD50 recruitment to DNA breaks. This mechanism counteracts cellular and tissue aging, extending lifespan in laboratory models. This signal is based on A cGAS-mediated mechanism in naked mole-rats potentiates DNA repair and delays aging. from PubMed. Read the original report for full context.
